messages.text:
"I want to make a top down 3rd person RPG. The concept is a frustrated father raising 3 daughters. The girls are smart yet unruly and witting. The father has to accomplish household chores and attempt to get the 3 girls to help. He has to use his own wit and cleverness to get the girls to do chores. There is also a great pyrenees named Charlie who appears at times and adds to the chaos. he has the personality of a sterotypical great pyrenees. the girls names are Elaina, who is 12, elsie who is 9, and ellerie who is 5. The game starts in the morning with father in bed and the girls getting up at different times and waking up. he has to feed them, or convince them to work together to make breakfast for them selves. some of the tasks that need done are showers, doing laundry and dishes, etc. The day progresses to getting everyone in bed at night and everyone asleep. You win the game when everyone is asleep. Some things to take into consideration are everyones focus, and dad needs mental health breaks occassonally without losing his temper. If dad loses his temper too many times you lose the game. There should be on screen controls with buttons and arrows to move the dad around. The children characters on screen move on their own according to whatever each characters agenda is. the house should have 2 bedrooms. the girls all share one bedroom, the father has one bedroom. there is a bathroom with washer and dryer in it, and a kitchen and a living room. there are various distractions for the girls such as toys, tv, books and sometimes escaping outside. the girls also need breaks occasionally where they are allowed a distraction in order to stay on task.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete playable top-down third-person RPG about a frustrated father managing three daughters, chores, distractions, and household chaos.

## Requirements
- Start in the father’s bed in the morning.
- Include Elaina (12), Elsie (9), Ellerle (5), and Charlie the Great Pyrenees.
- Include two bedrooms, bathroom with washer/dryer, kitchen, living room, and door passages between rooms.
- Provide chores such as breakfast, showers, laundry, dishes, and bedtime.
- Add autonomous child agendas and distractions: toys, TV, books, and escaping outside.
- Track focus and dad mental health; too much temper loss loses the game.
- Winning condition is everyone asleep in bed.
- Add visible on-screen movement controls and D-pad-style arrows for tablets and phones.
- Keep the entire playable screen within a horizontal tablet viewport without scrolling.
- Ensure the dad can escape from the bedroom and move throughout the house.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a single-page browser game with a top-down illustrated house scene.
- Added a responsive canvas layout, sidebar dashboard, touch controls, character movement, room interactions, chores, timers, stats, win/loss states, and restart functionality.
- Added clickable/touch room passage areas and keyboard movement support.

## Work State
### Completed
- Complete playable game concept and implementation were requested.
- Initial HTML/CSS/JavaScript game build was created.
- Gameplay, characters, tasks, distractions, movement controls, stats, and win/loss logic were added.
- Responsive tablet-oriented layout was requested as a correction.
- Door passage support between rooms was requested as a correction.

### Active
- Ensuring the latest implementation fully displays the entire playable area in horizontal tablet orientation.
- Verifying that door passages and room boundaries no longer trap the father in the bedroom.

### Blocked
- [none]

## Next Move
1. Open `index.html` in the deployed browser and verify it renders a fully playable horizontal layout.
2. Test all door passages by moving the father from the bedroom into the hallway and adjacent rooms.
3. Verify touch D-pad and keyboard controls, chores, win/loss conditions, and tablet viewport fit.
4. Capture a screenshot for visual confirmation.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main and likely only browser game implementation.

## Important Context
- The father must be able to leave the bedroom from the start; bedroom exits and room doorways must remain passable.
- The playable area must fit within the tablet viewport horizontally with no page scrolling.

README.md
## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Created `index.html` with a playable top-down house, visible door openings, and matching collision gaps so Dad can walk out of his bedroom and between rooms. It also includes keyboard and on-screen touch controls, chores, household status, and win/loss states.

I checked the game script syntax and captured a browser render. I couldn’t verify movement interactively because Playwright’s Chromium browser isn’t installed in this environment.
